ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Question: 437
A school class is going on a class trip, and a vote is being taken of where the class wants to go. The school expects that half of the students would want to go to Disney World, while the other half would want to go to visit Washington, DC Despite these expectations, only 42 students wanted to go to Washington, DC, while twice as many wanted to go to Disney World. Which of the following correctly identifies the chi-square statistic?

method.method_draft: Compute everything directly from the text. The text says 42 students chose Washington, DC, and twice as many chose Disney World, so Disney World has 84 students. The total is 42 + 84 = 126. The expectation is half for each destination, so the expected count is 126 / 2 = 63 for each. Apply chi-square: for Washington, (42 - 63)^2 / 63 = 441 / 63 = 7; for Disney, (84 - 63)^2 / 63 = 441 / 63 = 7. Sum the contributions: 7 + 7 = 14.
method.CoT_raw: Compute directly from the text. The actual count for Washington, DC is 42 students. Twice as many wanted Disney World, so Disney World has 2 × 42 = 84 students. The total number of students is 42 + 84 = 126. The expected split is half for each destination, so the expected count for each is 126 / 2 = 63. For Washington, the chi-square contribution is (42 - 63)^2 / 63 = (-21)^2 / 63 = 441 / 63 = 7. For Disney World, the contribution is (84 - 63)^2 / 63 = 21^2 / 63 = 441 / 63 = 7. The chi-square statistic is 7 + 7 = 14.
